findings.evidence: catalog-proposal.json explicitly states proposal_catalog_not_yet_an_index_or_selector; all six entries disclose that semantic types are not currently enforced by runtime string validation. Each names fixed-template execution, bounded result counts, empty-view semantics and nonclaims. The composition section warns that compatible types do not verify intent and unsupported schedule/load/delivery subquestions remain unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Ready as a design proposal only. Actual runtime conformance, output binding fidelity, resource usage and performance remain unverified because executable source and checks are outside this packet.

findings.evidence: The two composition hints propagate only order.id and machine.id. Shared version_binding text names snapshot/source_sha256/as_of, but the hints do not state a checked same-snapshot join invariant or same-record product/capability/date predicate. inspect_entity relations is an empty list despite its description promising relation direction; the meaning of empty relations is not specified. These are design underspecifications, not demonstrated implementation defects.
findings.recommendation: Before implementation, specify same-snapshot evidence joins, order requirement retention, single-record date/product/capability checks and directional relation support. Keep them distinct from typed identifier compatibility and from unavailable source completeness.

findings.evidence: The proposed comparison gives all arms the same catalog information, decomposition, access and aggregate budgets, but the full-catalog, retrieval, and retrieval-plus-constraints arms can still differ in visible context length, filtering, search overhead and consumed generator budget. A six-item catalog and old12 development cases cannot establish scalable retrieval or independent evaluation benefits.
findings.recommendation: In the future frozen protocol record exact presented metadata, retrieval and generation costs, abstention behavior and budget exhaustion; distinguish lexical from dense retrieval and new compositions from novel independent domains. No present efficacy or implementation benchmark claim is warranted.
